narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the amount in your savings. Your checking account status had the largest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having a negative balance puts you in a relatively small group—only 12.6% of approved applicants show a negative checking account—signaling higher risk to the bank. Your savings level also worked against you, as having less than 100 DM is common among higher-risk cases and further increased the predicted risk.

Working in your favor was the shorter 12-month duration you requested. Approved applicants typically ask for almost 20 months on average, so your more modest term helped reduce the risk score. Unfortunately, these positive effects were not enough to offset the concerns raised by your account status and limited savings.

You should focus on improving your checking account balance and building your savings over the next few months. Once your financial buffers are stronger, reapply. This is the most direct way to improve your chances with the model. (218 words)
